# Isolated table-border reference controls

The original twelve-page DOCX is generated by
`tools/isolated_table_border_fixture.py` using python-docx and direct OOXML.
It contains no corpus content or embedded fonts. The reference application opened it
read-only and exported `native.pdf` without saving the source. Source and PDF
SHA-256 hashes bind the independent PDFium vector measurements recorded by
`tools/record_isolated_table_border.py` in `reference.json`.

Controls use compatibility mode 15, Letter paper, one-inch margins, Arial
12pt, exact 18pt heading lines, a 288pt table and zero cell margins unless
specified. They vary omitted/AutoFit/fixed layout, empty/text cells, margins,
1/4.5/8pt solid borders, left/right corner joins, two columns and two rows.
The first control also appears in every page header.

The reference application extends the exposed left end of an outer solid bottom border by about
0.75pt. Top borders and internal row borders do not extend. A visible left
border uses the normal corner join. These controls support a paint-only
compatibility rule; ECMA-376 Part 1 section 17.4.66 describes table borders
but does not prescribe this one-pixel cap. Table widths, content placement,
row heights and editing geometry must remain unchanged.

The browser test compares header/body ink bounds on every page within
0.15pt, plus 0.0001pt for PDFium float32 rounding at the boundary. It also
checks exact no-edit package preservation, unrelated parts after an edit,
exact undo, editable reopening and the twelve-page count. Unit controls
check the individual caps, adjacent segments and unchanged height prepass.
